plants.name: Cornus florida
plants.description: A graceful, layered small tree whose branches are covered in broad, notched, petal-like bracts. They float above the bare woodland understory like pale butterflies. The true flowers are tiny greenish clusters in the center of each bract.
plants.location: Eastern United States, in woodlands, gardens and streetsides from the mid-Atlantic to the South
plants.funFact: What look like four big petals are actually modified leaves called bracts. They protect the cluster of small true flowers at the center.

plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: Satin-smooth, cup-shaped blooms stand upright on sturdy stems in striped, flamed and solid colors. Mid-April is peak season in the Dutch bulb fields near Lisse, where the fields look like bands of paint stretching to the horizon.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early April to early May, peaking in mid-April
plants.location: The Netherlands, especially the bulb-growing region around Lisse and Keukenhof Gardens
plants.funFact: In 17th-century Holland, tulip bulbs were so coveted that prices soared during 'tulip mania.' Some single bulbs reportedly sold for more than a skilled craftsman earned in a year.

plants.name: Nerine bowdenii
plants.description: Slender, sturdy stems rise from the ground topped with spidery umbels of frilled, glittering pink flowers. They bring a late burst of color as the southern hemisphere heads into autumn. The petals have a crystalline sparkle in the sun.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn, January to May
plants.location: Eastern South Africa, native to the high mountain grasslands and rocky slopes of the Drakensberg region
plants.funFact: Nerine bowdenii is a summer-growing bulb from high mountains. Its flower stems often appear just as the leaves are dying back at the end of the growing season.
